messages.subject: Managing Users Gracefully
parts:
So I'm interested in what the best way is to manage users using R Shiny Pro. Two topics:
  1. Restricting logins per accounts gracefully
  2. Closing idle connections gracefully
For #1. Can you use LDAP to query connections, or should I use a database to insert when new users log-in and query that? Then it would need to tell users to log-out from other connections in order to log-in (and/or enable them to log-out for the other connections).

For #2. We need to keep a value for app_idle_timeout because we have issues when two sessions with the same user are connected (also would have more issues once #1 is implemented...). I don't see a way to directly read and write the session's idle time but am I wrong? Ideally we could capture idle time and at a certain point initiate a pop-up that says "Would you like to continue your session? You have X seconds until your session will be closed". Then if they click continue the idle time is overridden. If their session is ended it should go to log-in screen with alternative text message saying "Your session ended, please log back in". Is it possible to display alternative text on the log-in screen at this juncture?

Thanks,

Chris

messages.author: bbc57ffa8a14ad13
messages.subject: Re: Managing Users Gracefully
parts:
Hi Chris,

For #1, am I understanding correctly that you want to restrict the global number of sessions a single user can have at once? If so, that's unfortunately not something that LDAP would be able to help with. You'd need to setup an extra system somewhere (could be as simple as a directory of files on your server or could be a whole web API) that would be able to track how many sessions each user currently has. You'd integrate with that system in your Shiny code by querying to see if the user should be allowed to open this new connection or not and kill the connection if not.

For #2, we unfortunately don't include this feature at the moment, but it is a request we've heard before and do plan to tackle. For the time being, however, you'd probably have to track the idle time yourself in JavaScript as you suggested, and you could disable the `app_idle_timeout` setting so you can just manage all of this on your own. I haven't stayed up-to-date on the various libraries people have put out there, but here's at least one that claims to be able to show alerts, if you're trying to minimize the amount of JS you have to write. https://github.com/AnalytixWare/ShinySky

Jeff
